findings: Hip and shoulder angular rates are computed independently from their own fixed-camera two-point axes; no shared native rotation is subtracted. Only wrist position is body-center relative.

The derivative uses real decoder PTS and five neighboring observations. Three fixed support observations on each side can support an acceleration-boundary peak; they cannot move the peak search outside the existing acceleration phase.
Short projected axes, insufficient movement, missing two-sided peak support and broad or multiple peak plateaus remain explicitly unmeasured. These measurement limits were not relaxed.
The discovered float boundary error could incorrectly call a one-frame difference resolved. The patch prevents that false measurement; it does not manufacture new timing coverage.

In the frozen real return, hip and shoulder peaks both occur at 8100 ms. Independent rates can legitimately have the same sampled maximum. Their order is unresolved at this video's frame/model resolution, rather than evidence of a software-enforced common peak.

ICS has a separated shoulder peak and an equal hip/wrist peak. The existing formula compares the adjacent hip-to-shoulder and shoulder-to-wrist relationships; its 60 result is unchanged. It is a projected-order proxy, not measured force or expert-calibrated kinetic-chain quality.
